title: Fibre degree bounds hold for all field-valued points (Stacks 03J5)
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $n\ge0$ an integer. The following are equivalent: (1) $n$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $f$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound]; (2) for every field $K$ and every morphism of schemes $\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the fibre product $X_K=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-fibre-product], regarded as a scheme over $K$ through its second projection $X_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, is finite over $K$ (the projection is a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]) and $\dim_K\Gamma(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})\le n$, where $\Gamma(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})$ is a $K$-algebra through the ring map induced by the projection.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), line 15322, equivalence of (1) and (2), and the first two sentences of its proof (line 15339: (2)=>(1) trivial, taking Spec kappa(y) -> Y; (1)=>(2) since X_K = Spec K x_{Spec kappa(y)} X_y for y the image of Spec K -> Y)

proof.text: For the reverse implication, apply the field-valued hypothesis with K=κ(y) and g=Y.fromSpecResidueField y. By def-pc-scheme-fibre the second projection is definitionally f.fiberToSpecResidueField y. Thus both clauses of def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound follow without changing the chosen pullback.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), statement at line 15322, proof at line 15339, first two sentences (equivalence of (1) and (2))

proof.text: For the forward implication fix K and g:Spec K→Y, set ξ=default and h=pullback.snd f g. The canonical map φ:K→κ_alg(ξ) is an isomorphism by Mathlib Ideal.algEquivResidueFieldOfField. Compose asIso φ with the inverse of Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso to obtain e:K≅κ_Spec K(ξ). Scheme.Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField and Spec.map_comp give Spec.map e.hom=fromSpecResidueField ξ. Hence this residue morphism is an isomorphism. Its pullback h.fiberι ξ is an isomorphism by the pullback-of-isomorphism instance.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), statement at line 15322, proof at line 15339, first two sentences (equivalence of (1) and (2))

proof.text: Apply finite_fiber_degree_pullback f g ξ to the finite fibre at g(ξ), supplied by the assumed bound. It gives finiteness of q=h.fiberToSpecResidueField ξ and equality of its degree with that original fibre. From h.fiber_fac and invertibility of p=h.fiberι ξ, obtain p⁻¹≫q≫Spec.map e.hom=h. Isomorphisms and finite morphisms compose, so h is finite.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), statement at line 15322, proof at line 15339, first two sentences (equivalence of (1) and (2))

proof.text: The already proved source-library lemma Scheme.Hom.finrankΓ_eq_of_iso h q (asIso p).symm e applies directly to p⁻¹≫q≫Spec.map e.hom=h. It gives h.finrankΓ=q.finrankΓ for the exact algebra structures in the bound definition. Transitivity with the degree equality from the preceding step and the assumed bound at g(ξ) proves h.finrankΓ≤n. No basis-transport theorem or separate field-base fibre-identification theorem is needed.
